welcomeHeadline: Choose which sites come first, and which you never see again.
welcomeLead: Anubis puts a small button next to every search result on Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, and others. Have a go on this practice search first. Nothing you do here is saved.
welcomeStepOpen: Press the button next to a result
welcomeStepRank: Put that site where you want it
welcomeStepHide: Hide a site you don't want
welcomeStepsAllDone: You've done all three. Your real searches work the same way.
welcomeTourPinned: $1 will come first whenever it shows up.
welcomeTourRaised: Anubis will raise $1 whenever it shows up.
welcomeTourLowered: Anubis will lower $1 whenever it shows up.
welcomeTourOpen: Anubis puts this $1 button next to every result. You'd probably trust $2 more than someone's lecture notes, but it's stuck in third. Press the button next to it.
welcomeTourRank: From here you can move $1 up, down, or off the page. Pin it to keep it at the top.
welcomeTourFind: Next, find a site you don't want to see and press its $1.
welcomeTourHide: Press Hide and you won't see $1 again.
welcomeTourDone: It's gone. Anubis always says what it hid above the results, and Undo brings it back. Look for the $1 on your next search.
welcomeMoreHow: You don't need any of these, but each one is worth a look.
welcomeTagsWhat: Put your own labels on sites.
welcomeTagsMore: A tag can move every site that has it. Trusted raises them and Sign-up wall lowers them.
welcomeListsWhat: Use lists that other people keep up to date.
welcomeListsHow: Switch these off and on to see the tags change.
welcomeListsMore: You can turn them off or add more in the settings.
welcomePanelsWhat: Get rid of AI answers and other clutter.
welcomePanelsMore: Anubis leaves these alone until you say otherwise. Pick what to remove in the settings.
welcomePinWhy: You don't need it, but it's handy. It lets you rank the site you're on and see what Anubis did to a search.
welcomePinChrome: Press the puzzle piece next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.
welcomePinEdge: Press the puzzle piece next to the address bar, then the eye beside Anubis.
welcomePinOpera: Press the cube next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.
welcomePinFirefox: Press the puzzle piece, then the gear beside Anubis, and choose Pin to Toolbar.
welcomePinAndroid: Anubis is in the browser's menu, under Extensions.
syncIntro: Your sites and settings on your other computers and browsers.
syncFirefox: Firefox syncs your sites and settings when you're signed in with Add-ons ticked in its sync settings.
syncFirefoxAndroid: Firefox for Android doesn't sync add-on data. Connect a WebDAV server below to sync.
syncChrome: Your browser syncs your sites and settings when you're signed in with extensions syncing.
syncTooBig: Your list is too big for sync, so it stays on this device. Settings still sync.
webdavIntro: To sync between Firefox and Chrome, connect the same WebDAV storage in each, such as Koofr, InfiniCLOUD, or Nextcloud.
webdavHelp: Where to get an address and a password
webdavAddressHint: The service's WebDAV address, starting with https://
listPermissionDenied: Anubis needs permission to read $1 to update this list.
webdavPasswordHint: Use an app password if the service offers one.
webdavEncrypt: Encrypt the sync file end to end (recommended)
webdavEncryptionHint: At least 12 characters, the same in every browser. It never leaves this browser, and can't be recovered.
webdavCorrectPassphraseHint: Use the passphrase you set in the other browser.
webdavChangePassphraseHint: Then enter the new passphrase in your other browsers.
webdavChangePassphraseHelp: What happens when you change it
webdavEncryptionShort: Use an encryption passphrase of at least 12 characters.
webdavEncrypted: Encrypted end to end. The server can't read it, and a forgotten passphrase can't be recovered.
webdavEncryptionPending: Encryption is set up. The next sync encrypts the server copy.
webdavEncryptionMissing: Enter the passphrase from your other browser to read an encrypted file.
webdavPrivacy: With encryption off, the server can read the sync file.
webdavBadAddress: Enter the service's WebDAV address, starting with https://
webdavMissingLogin: Enter the user name and password too.
webdavDenied: Anubis needs your permission to send your list to $1.
webdavWhen: Syncs a few seconds after a change, at startup, and when you search.
webdavDisconnected: Disconnected. Your data stays here and on the server.
webdavErrorAuth: The server didn't accept the login. Try an app password.
webdavErrorForbidden: The server doesn't let this account save files there.
webdavErrorFolder: There's no folder at that address.
webdavErrorPermission: Anubis lost permission to sync with $1. Press Sync now to allow it.
webdavErrorNetwork: Couldn't reach $1. Check the address and your connection.
webdavErrorFile: Anubis can't read the anubis-sync.json there, so it left it alone. Use another folder.
webdavErrorNeedsPassphrase: This sync file is encrypted. Enter its passphrase.
webdavErrorUnencrypted: The server's sync file is no longer encrypted. It was left unchanged.
webdavErrorChanged: The sync file changed meanwhile. Nothing was overwritten. Sync, then try again.
webdavErrorUnconfirmed: The connection to $1 dropped while saving. If the next sync says the passphrase is wrong, enter the new one.
